meta.scope: UAE Batch 3 — Dubai–Abu Dhabi contrast, logistics/ports, and tourism densification.

candidates.title: Dubai economic and logistics framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from FCSC and Dubai monitoring sources
candidates.description: Framing of Dubai as the principal non-oil, services, logistics, tourism and finance hub. Dominates container throughput (Jebel Ali), visitor arrivals, trade facilitation and private-sector services activity within the federation.
candidates.notes: Primary Dubai densification. Complements the federal non-oil structure.

candidates.title: Abu Dhabi economic and hydrocarbon framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from FCSC and Abu Dhabi sources
candidates.description: Framing of Abu Dhabi as the principal hydrocarbon, sovereign-wealth and capital emirate. Hosts the bulk of oil and gas production, ADNOC, ADIA/Mubadala and the federal capital functions.
candidates.notes: Primary Abu Dhabi densification. Complements the federal hydrocarbon core.

candidates.title: Ports and container throughput statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from DP World and logistics sources
candidates.description: Statistics on container and cargo throughput, centred on Jebel Ali and other UAE ports. The UAE is a major global transshipment and logistics node; throughput is continuously referenced in trade, diversification and regional-hub analysis.
candidates.notes: Core logistics densification under global-hub structure.

candidates.title: Tourism and visitor-arrival statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from Dubai DET and national sources
candidates.description: Statistics on overnight visitor arrivals and tourism performance. Dubai is the dominant destination; multi-million annual arrivals support a large hospitality, retail and transport services base.
candidates.notes: Core tourism densification under services-diversification structure.

candidates.title: UAE Dubai–Abu Dhabi–logistics–tourism densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from emirate and sector sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding Dubai framing, Abu Dhabi framing, ports/logistics statistics and tourism statistics into a coherent dual-emirate and services-hub layer.
